name: Terminal Semantics & System Gotchas
description: Expert Linux shell and systems reasoning, inspired by hard Terminal-Bench task themes (permissions/ACLs, tar determinism, git forensics, date normalization, log aggregation, HTML/text processing, SQLite WAL, cron semantics, bash pipefail, packaging conflicts, locale sorting, filesystem edge cases). Every canonical answer was produced by executing the scenario on Ubuntu 24.04 (bash 5.x, GNU coreutils/findutils/sed/tar/git, mawk, sqlite3 3.45, Python 3.12 zoneinfo) — never written by hand. Graded exactly on the final ANSWER line.

prompts.title: Effective permissions after setfacl + chmod mask recalc
prompts.description: Predict stat mode and effective ACL permissions after mask recalculation. Use numeric IDs u:1042/g:2088 (no passwd entry, shown as 1042/2088).

messages.content:
You are a Linux systems expert. Determine the exact output/behavior described. You may reason as long as you need, but you MUST end your reply with a single final line in exactly this form:
ANSWER: <output>
where <output> is precisely what is asked for (no quotes, no code fences).

You run exactly these commands in order on Ubuntu 24.04 (GNU coreutils, getfacl 2.3):
mkdir data && chmod 0754 data
touch data/report.csv && chmod 640 data/report.csv
setfacl -m u:1042:rwx,g:2088:rx,other::--- data/
setfacl -d -m u:1042:rX,g:2088:rX data/
# state 1
stat -c %a data
# then
chmod 0754 data
# state 2
stat -c %a data
getfacl data | grep "user:1042"

What are: stat %a after state 1, stat %a after state 2, and the effective permission bits for user 1042 on data after state 2?
Give them as comma-separated: <stat1>,<stat2>,<effective>
Example: 777,755,rwx
